_about: Knowledge base id map, reviewed by hand (docs/ai/schema.md §3). `legacy` maps old source ids to kb document ids. `protocols` gives each protocol its document id. `keywords` are plain-language words people use for a document; they are indexed for lexical search only and never shown or quoted. `notes` is extra card text (how to read a self-test score); it is illustrative and not clinically reviewed. `versions` overrides the document version (default 1; protocols take theirs from protocols.json).

notes.TEST-PVT: A slower reaction time than your own normal, or more lapses, points to tiredness you may not feel yet. It is a reason to rest, not a diagnosis.
notes.TEST-DSST: Fewer correct matches than your own normal can follow short sleep, stress or distraction. One low score means little; a trend means more.
notes.TEST-SPAN: Holding fewer digits than usual can follow short sleep or a heavy workload. It is compared with your own normal, never with others.
notes.TEST-MOOD: Mood and stress are each rated 1 to 5. A hard day counts the same as a good one. A run of low mood or high stress is worth talking about with the medical officer.
notes.TEST-KSS: Scores go from 1 to 9: 1 extremely alert, 2 very alert, 3 alert, 4 rather alert, 5 neither alert nor sleepy, 6 some signs of sleepiness, 7 sleepy with no effort to stay awake, 8 sleepy with some effort to stay awake, 9 very sleepy and fighting sleep. A score of 7 or more means reactions are slower than they feel: hand over critical or precise work and rest if you can.
notes.TEST-TLX: Workload is scored 0 to 100 from six ratings. A higher score means more demanding work. It describes the day, not you.
notes.TEST-WELLBEING: PHQ-2 (low mood) and GAD-2 (worry) each go from 0 to 6. A score of 3 or more on either is worth talking about with the medical officer. It is a short screen, not a diagnosis.
notes.TEST-VITALS: Pulse, pressure, temperature and oxygen are compared with your own normal from before launch. A single reading outside it is a reason to measure again, not a diagnosis.
notes.TEST-AMSLER: All lines straight is the expected result. Wavy, missing or blurred lines are a reason to repeat the test the next day and to tell the medical officer, because they can signal a change at the back of the eye linked to fluid shift.
notes.TEST-SYMPTOMS: Each symptom gets a severity from 1 to 5. A severity of 3 or more is worth a look by the medical officer even when the sensors look normal.
notes.TEST-SLEEP: Hours are counted from bedtime to waking, with a 1 to 5 quality rating. Less than 7 hours slows reactions before you feel it.
notes.TEST-READING: Reading for 20 minutes or more counts as the daily reading goal.
notes.TEST-JOURNAL: Only the fact that you wrote and the number of lines are saved. The text never leaves the screen.
